title: Water Cycle Basics
summary: This lesson explores how water moves above and below the Earth's surface through the continuous process of the water cycle. Students will examine the four main stages: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection.

sections.text: Scene: A diagram on a light blue background displays arrows forming a circular loop above and below the Earth's surface. The arrows trace the continuous movement of water through different states.
Scene: A bright yellow sun at the top of the page sends heat rays down to liquid water, turning it into vapor. Higher up in the cool sky, that vapor transforms into fluffy white clouds.
Scene: Darkened clouds release blue droplets of rain and white flakes of snow falling back down to the ground. Below, the runoff gathers together into blue rivers, lakes, and oceans.

key_concepts: Water cycle movement above and below the Earth surface
Evaporation using heat from the sun
Condensation forming clouds when vapor cools high in the sky
Precipitation returning water as rain or snow
Collection gathering runoff into rivers, lakes and oceans
learning_objectives: Describe how water moves above and below the Earth surface
Identify the four stages of the water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection
